PITC is a degradation product of DPTU and appears to be a potent elicitor of contact allergy.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Finn Chambers (8 mm) on Scanpor tape, applied on upper back for 48 h; readings on days 3 or 4 and 7 (or days 2 and 4 in Turku); vehicle: petrolatum; concentrations tested: 1.0%, 0.5%, 0.1%, 0.01%, 0.001% (w/w in pet.).
evidence.support_text: Table 1 presents patch-test results for diphenylthiourea (DPTU) in 8 DPTU-allergic participants. DPTU at concentrations from 1.0% to 0.001% (w/w in petrolatum) elicited positive reactions (+, ++, +++) in most participants, with some equivocal ('?') or negative results at the lowest concentrations. The strongest reaction at any reading (D3/D4 or D7) is recorded. Commercially available DPTU (DPTU-com) at 1% also gave positive reactions. These results demonstrate that DPTU elicits allergic contact dermatitis in sensitized individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Germany, 1992–2003; 134 patients; 1% in pet.; metalworkers with suspected occupational contact dermatitis
evidence.support_text: In a German study from 1992–2003, 134 metalworkers with suspected occupational contact dermatitis were patch tested with N,N'-methylenebis(5-methyloxazolidine) 1% in pet.; 6.7% had positive reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test with MEA 2% in petrolatum, reading at day 3; control population: non-metalworkers (n=452).
evidence.support_text: Patch test reactions at D3 to MEA 2% pet. in the control group (non-metalworkers, n=452) showed 1.3% + reactions and no ++ reactions. The authors note the diagnostic quality is questioned, and positive reactions may indicate irritation rather than contact allergy (reference from preceding text).
